citation: An Update on the Phenotype, Genotype and Neurobiology of ADCY5-Related Disease. (PMID: 33934385)
summary: ADCY5 encodes adenylyl cyclase 5, the enzyme responsible for conversion of ATP to cAMP. ADCY5 is the most commonly expressed isoform of adenylyl cyclase in medium spiny neurons (MSNs) of the striatum and integrates and controls dopaminergic signaling. Through the cAMP pathway, ADCY5 is a key regulator of cortical and thalamic signaling that controls initiation of voluntary movements and prevention of involuntary movements. Gain-of-function mutations lead to dysregulation of the cAMP pathway, reduced inhibitory activity, and involuntary hyperkinetic movements.

citation: New genetic loci implicated in fasting glucose homeostasis and their impact on type 2 diabetes risk. (PMID: 20081858)
sample_size: 46,186 nondiabetic participants with follow-up in 76,558 additional subjects
summary: GWAS meta-analysis of 46,186 nondiabetic participants identified ADCY5 as a novel locus associated with fasting glucose and HOMA-B (beta-cell function). ADCY5 was also demonstrated to be associated with type 2 diabetes risk. The locus contains a gene variant influencing signal transduction and glucose-sensing.

citation: Requirement of Zebrafish Adcy3a and Adcy5 in Melanosome Dispersion and Melanocyte Stripe Formation. (PMID: 36430661)
summary: In zebrafish, adcy3a-/- and adcy5-/- double mutants cause defects in melanosome dispersion and impair adult melanocyte stripe formation. Mechanistically, Adcy3a and Adcy5 regulate melanosome dispersion by activating kinesin-1 while inhibiting cytoplasmic dynein-1. In adult zebrafish, Adcy3a and Adcy5 regulate expression of Mitfa and melanin synthesis enzymes (Tyr, Dct, Trp1b). These proteins mediate α-MSH-MC1R/cAMP-PKA signaling.

citation: PDE10A and ADCY5 mutations linked to molecular and microstructural basal ganglia pathology. (PMID: 30345538)
sample_size: 6 subjects with PDE10A and ADCY5 mutations

ADCY5 mutations were associated with decreased PDE10A expression in striatum and globus pallidus, decreased dopamine transporter expression in striatum, loss of substantia nigra neuromelanin-containing neurons, and microstructural white and gray matter changes within striatocortical pathways.

citation: ADCY5 gene expression in adipose tissue is related to obesity in men and mice. (PMID: 25793868)
summary: In humans, visceral ADCY5 mRNA expression is significantly higher in obese compared to lean individuals and correlates with BMI, body fat mass, circulating leptin, fat distribution, waist and hip circumference. In mice, Adcy5 expression in adipose tissue is significantly higher after high-fat diet compared to chow. However, rs11708067 is not associated with ADCY5 mRNA expression levels in either fat depot, suggesting the SNP's T2D association may not be mediated through altered adipose tissue ADCY5 expression.

citation: Genome-wide discovery of genetic loci that uncouple excess adiposity from its comorbidities. (PMID: 33619380)
summary: GWAS identified 62 loci where the same allele is associated with higher adiposity and lower cardiometabolic risk. ADCY5 was prioritized as a gene affecting insulin-glucose signaling in adipocytes. The study suggests ADCY5 may represent a therapeutic target to reduce cardiometabolic risk linked to excess adiposity.

citation: ASHG 2015 - A functional regulatory variant associated with type 2 diabetes and fasting glucose levels at the ADCY5 locus.
summary: The rs11708067-A T2D risk allele shows decreased enhancer activity compared to rs11708067-G in luciferase reporter assays in 832/13 rat insulinoma cells (1.3 to 3-fold difference, p=0.0017-0.03). Allelic imbalance in H3K27ac ChIP-seq and differential protein binding in EMSAs support rs11708067-A as a functional variant. RNA-seq from 82 published and 32 new islet samples showed decreased ADCY5 expression for rs11708067-A (p=6.5×10⁻¹³).

citation: ASHG 2017 - An epigenetic switch confers pleiotropic risk for bone mineral density and hyperglycaemia.
summary: In patient-derived osteoblasts and primary adipocytes, ADCY5 downregulation (mediated by loss of SREBF motif at rs56371916) leads to perturbation of fatty acid oxidation during early differentiation (3.6-fold, p=0.003) and failure to differentiate (2.9-fold change in alkaline phosphatase, p=0.0014). In adipocytes, ADCY5 downregulation decreases adrenergic lipolysis rate (1.9-fold, p=0.0012). CRISPR C-to-T editing restored ADCY5 activation and osteoblast differentiation.

citation: Heroin Regulates Orbitofrontal Circular RNAs. (PMID: 35163373)
sample_size: Male and female rats with heroin self-administration
summary: Microarray analysis identified circAdcy5 as a heroin-responsive circular RNA in the rat orbitofrontal cortex after heroin self-administration. Linear Adcy5 mRNA levels were significantly changed by heroin exposure. circAdcy5 may impact cellular processes contributing to neurobiological adaptations from chronic heroin exposure through circRNA:microRNA sponging mechanisms.

citation: ASHG 2015 - The impact of known type 2 diabetes associated variants on circulating levels of GLP-1, GIP and glucagon during an oral glucose tolerance test.
summary: The ADCY5 rs11708067 risk allele was associated with increased incremental area under the curve (iAUC) of plasma glucagon from 0 to 30 minutes during OGTT (Beta [SE]: 0.130 [0.043], p=0.0025), showing reduced repression of glucagon release after an oral glucose load. This suggests ADCY5 variants affect alpha-cell function and glucagon secretion.

summary: GABRA1 is a functional target of puerarin, a natural compound that suppresses the DMV-vagus pathway. citation: Genetic variations in GABA metabolism and epilepsy (PMID: 35850019)
summary: GABRA1 encodes a GABA receptor subunit and is a key member of GABAergic neurotransmission pathways. Mutations in GABRA1 lead to epilepsy syndromes primarily by downregulating receptor expression and reducing the amplitude of GABA-evoked potentials, establishing its role in inhibitory neurotransmission.

citation: An airway-to-brain sensory pathway mediates influenza-induced sickness (PMID: 36890237)
summary: Petrosal GABRA1 neurons form a primary airway-to-brain sensory pathway that detects locally produced prostaglandins (PGE2) and mediates systemic sickness responses to respiratory virus infection. Ablating petrosal GABRA1 neurons eliminates influenza-induced decreases in food intake, water intake, and mobility during early-stage infection.

citation: Network pharmacology screening, in vitro and in vivo evaluation of antianxiety and antidepressant drug-food analogue (PMID: 39241390)

citation: The Genetic Landscape of Epilepsy of Infancy with Migrating Focal Seizures (PMID: 31618474)
summary: De novo dominant GABRA1 mutations were identified as novel genetic causes of epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures (EIMFS), a severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy. GABRA1 variants contribute to the genetic heterogeneity of EIMFS with diverse molecular mechanisms.

citation: GABRA1-Related Disorders: From Genetic to Functional Pathways (PMID: 37606373)
summary: GABRA1 variants display both loss-of-function (LoF) and gain-of-function (GoF) effects depending on structural position within the subunit. Variants in extracellular domains cause mild phenotypes with LoF effects, while variants in transmembrane helices cause severe phenotypes with either GoF or LoF effects, establishing genotype-phenotype correlations.

citation: Understanding paralogous epilepsy-associated GABA(A) receptor variants: Clinical implications, mechanisms, and potential pitfalls (PMID: 39642202)
summary: GABRA1 M1 proline missense variants (α1P260L, α1P260S) cause gain-of-function effects by increasing GABA sensitivity 3- to 23-fold in α1β2/3γ2 receptors. These variants are associated with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with early seizure onset, demonstrating that paralogous variants in GABRA1 lead to overall GOF traits.

citation: ASHG 2018 - Dissecting heterogeneity of neurodevelopmental disorders using seed centric genetic modules (J.C. Chow et al.)
significance: Significant enrichment of de novo mutations within modules (p<0.05)
summary: GABRA1 serves as a seed gene for constructing functional modules associated with epilepsy. Modules seeded with GABRA1 are significantly associated with long-term potentiation, synaptic vesicle cycle, and calcium signaling pathways, revealing its role in synaptic plasticity networks.

citation: ASHG 2018 - Whole exome sequencing in epilepsy reveals significant gene burden of ultra-rare deleterious variants (Y. Feng, EPI Collaborative)
summary: GABRA1 showed significant association with genetic generalized epilepsy (GGE) in the Epi25 Consortium's large WES study of 4,443 GGE patients and 17,668 controls. GABRA1 ranked among the strongest associations for GGE with OR=21.5 (p=3e-04), confirming its role in common epilepsy susceptibility.

summary: GABRA1 was identified as a gene carrying damaging de novo variants in cryptogenic cerebral palsy patients, with clinical overlap to autism and intellectual disability. This finding illustrates GABRA1's broader role in neurodevelopmental disorders beyond epilepsy.

citation: IRF2BPL inhibits proliferation, migration and invasion of osteosarcoma cells by inhibiting FOSL2-mediated PI3K/AKT pathway activation (PMID: 40834975)

citation: IRF2BPL transcriptionally regulates IGFBP2 to promote tumor progression and suppresses immune cell infiltration in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 41413713)

citation: IRF2BPL Is Associated with Neurological Phenotypes (PMID: 30057031)

citation: ASHG 2019 - Unravelling the mechanism underlying IRF2BPL in a neurodevelopmental disorder with regression, abnormal movements, loss of speech, and seizures

citation: Integrated analysis using methylation and gene expression microarrays reveals PDE4C as a prognostic biomarker in human glioma. (PMID: 24842301)
sample_size: 124 patient samples (56 low-grade, 63 high-grade glioma, 5 normal brain)
significance: Hypermethylation and reduced PDE4C expression associated with grade progression and overall survival (p<0.05)
summary: PDE4C exhibits promoter hypermethylation and reduced expression in high-grade gliomas compared to low-grade gliomas and normal brain. PDE4C functions as a tumor suppressor by promoting apoptosis through the wild-type p53 pathway and inhibiting cell migration in U87 glioma cells.

citation: HNF4α-Mediated LINC02560 Promotes Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma Progression by Targeting the miR-505-5p/PDE4C Axis. (PMID: 40427523)
sample_size: PTC tissues and KTC-1, BCPAP cell lines
significance: LINC02560 upregulation correlates with poor prognosis; functional assays demonstrate effects on proliferation, migration, and invasion
summary: PDE4C is a target of miR-505-5p; the long non-coding RNA LINC02560 acts as a competing endogenous RNA to sponge miR-505-5p and relieve suppression of PDE4C, thereby activating P-AKT and EMT signaling pathways in papillary thyroid carcinoma cells. HNF4α transcriptionally enhances LINC02560 expression.

citation: Cancer: Phosphodiesterase type 4C (PDE4C), the forgotten subfamily as a therapeutic target. (PMID: 37499270)
summary: PDE4C is a member of the phosphodiesterase type 4 (PDE4) enzyme family that specifically hydrolyzes cAMP in cell signaling systems. PDE4C has a restricted distribution pattern and is the least characterized of the four PDE4 subfamilies (A, B, C, D), with potential roles in cancer development.

citation: Elevated PDE4C level serves as a candidate diagnostic biomarker and correlates with poor survival in thyroid carcinoma. (PMID: 38514754)
significance: Higher PDE4C expression associated with shorter PFS (p<0.05)
summary: PDE4C expression is significantly upregulated in thyroid carcinoma tissues compared to normal tissues, and elevated PDE4C correlates with shorter progression-free survival. PDE4C participates in cAMP metabolic process by regulating adenylate cyclases (ADCY1, ADCY5, ADCY6, ADCY8, ADCY9) and affects immune cell infiltration during THCA progression.

citation: Analysis of the effects of M2 macrophage-derived PDE4C on the prognosis, metastasis and immunotherapy benefit of osteosarcoma. (PMID: 38774995)
sample_size: GSE162454 scRNA-seq profile; OS tissues and THP-1 cell line
significance: Positive correlation between PDE4C levels and M2 macrophage infiltration; elevated PDE4C associated with poor prognosis and metastasis
summary: PDE4C is transferred from M2 macrophages to osteosarcoma cells via exosomes and increases OS cell proliferation and mobility by upregulating collagen expression. Elevated PDE4C correlates with unfavorable prognosis, metastasis, increased TIDE score, and reduced immunotherapy response.

citation: Expression and function of phosphodiesterases (PDEs) in the rat urinary bladder. (PMID: 28687079)
significance: PDE4C not detected by RT-PCR/western blot in rat bladder
summary: PDE4C mRNA and protein were not detected in adult rat urinary bladder tissue, in contrast to other PDE isoforms (PDE4A, PDE4B, PDE4D) which were expressed. This indicates PDE4C has a restricted tissue distribution pattern.

citation: PDE4C stabilized by ELAVL1 promotes lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid cancer. (PMID: 41868681)
sample_size: PTC tissues and BCPAP, TPC-1 cell lines; mouse xenograft model
significance: PDE4C and ELAVL1 upregulated in PTC tissues; knockdown effects demonstrated by CCK-8, Transwell, and in vivo assays
summary: ELAVL1 (embryonic lethal abnormal vision like 1) directly interacts with PDE4C mRNA and increases PDE4C mRNA stability, promoting lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma. Knockdown of PDE4C suppresses cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and lymph node metastasis in vivo.

citation: The plasma peptides of Alzheimer's disease. (PMID: 34182925)
sample_size: AD patients, normal controls, and multiple disease controls (MS, ovarian cancer, breast cancer, sepsis, heart attack)
significance: PDE4C phosphopeptides showed increased observation frequency in AD plasma by Chi Square analysis with FDR correction
summary: Increased frequency of tryptic phosphopeptides from PDE4C were observed in plasma samples from Alzheimer's disease patients compared to controls and other disease states, suggesting altered PDE4C phosphorylation status in AD.

citation: Developmental and epilepsy spectrum of KCNB1 encephalopathy with long-term outcome (PMID: 32954514)
variant_detail: Multiple KCNB1 pathogenic variants (missense and truncating)
phenotype: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE); Developmental encephalopathy (DE); Infantile onset seizures; Late onset epilepsy; Severe to profound intellectual disability (67%); Autistic features (56%); Cognitive impairment; Poor long-term psychiatric and behavioral outcome
diagnostic_reason: Pathogenic variants identified through international collaboration; missense variants associated with more frequent and severe epilepsy compared to truncating variants
center_country: International collaboration with support from KCNB1 France family association

citation: Adaptive behavior and psychiatric comorbidities in KCNB1 encephalopathy (PMID: 34915430)
phenotype: Intellectual disability; Behavioral disturbances; Epilepsies of various severity; Pathological adaptive behavior (mild to severe); Attention problems (50%); Autism spectrum disorder (72%); Stagnation and slowing of adaptive functioning with age
diagnostic_reason: Confirmed KCNB1 encephalopathy diagnosis; severity of epilepsy phenotype predicted severity of behavioral profile (sensitivity 70%, specificity 90.9%)

citation: A novel autism-associated KCNB1 mutation dramatically slows Kv2.1 potassium channel activation, deactivation and inactivation (PMID: 39135902)
phenotype: Developmental delay; Absence seizures; Autism spectrum disorder; Hypotonia; Dysmorphic features
diagnostic_reason: Heterozygous variant identified by whole exome sequencing; functional investigation revealed slowing of channel activation, deactivation, and inactivation; familial segregation confirmed (father is obligate carrier with autistic features)

citation: Epilepsy and neurobehavioral abnormalities in mice with a dominant-negative KCNB1 pathogenic variant (PMID: 33132203)
phenotype: Epileptic spasms; Atonic seizures; Focal seizures; Tonic-clonic seizures; Refractory seizures (resistant to standard antiepileptic drugs)
diagnostic_reason: De novo pathogenic variant identified in infant; demonstrated dominant negative effect on KV2.1 clustering at endoplasmic reticulum-plasma membrane junctions

citation: Gastrointestinal Symptoms and Channelopathy-Associated Epilepsy (PMID: 34181986)
phenotype: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE); Gastrointestinal symptoms (35% of KCNB1-DEE patients); Daily or weekly GI symptoms (73% of those with GI symptoms); Frequent or serious discomfort (32%); Frequent or serious appetite disturbances (14%)
diagnostic_reason: Confirmed KCNB1-DEE diagnosis; part of channelopathy-associated DEE cohort

citation: Altered neurological and neurobehavioral phenotypes in a mouse model of the recurrent KCNB1-p.R306C voltage-sensor variant (PMID: 38485094)
phenotype: Global developmental delays (mild to severe); Cognitive impairment; Abnormal EEG patterns; Epilepsy with variable age of onset and severity; Behavioral disturbances; Hyperactivity; Aggression; Autism spectrum disorder features
diagnostic_reason: Most frequently identified recurrent KCNB1 variant; located in S4 voltage-sensing transmembrane domain; affects voltage-sensing without affecting channel expression

citation: Characterization of a KCNB1 variant associated with autism, intellectual disability, and epilepsy (PMID: 29264390)
phenotype: Neurodevelopmental disorder; Epilepsy; Centrotemporal spikes on EEG; Autism; Intellectual disability
diagnostic_reason: Identified by clinical whole-exome sequencing; functional characterization revealed biophysical channel defects in homotetrameric and heterotetrameric channels; partial loss of function relative to wild-type

citation: Spectrum of K(V) 2.1 Dysfunction in KCNB1-Associated Neurodevelopmental Disorders (PMID: 31600826)
phenotype: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE); Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs); Altered current density; Shifts in voltage dependence of activation and/or inactivation; Reduced cell-surface expression (some variants)
diagnostic_reason: Pathogenic variants associated with DEE or other NDDs; diverse functional defects demonstrated through high-throughput functional assays

citation: Clinician's guide to genes associated with Rett-like phenotypes-Investigation of a Danish cohort and review of the literature (PMID: 29023665)
phenotype: Rett-like phenotype
diagnostic_reason: Pathogenic variant identified in Danish cohort of 35 patients with Rett-like phenotypes; first report linking KCNB1 to Rett-like phenotype

citation: ASHG 2015 - Whole exome sequencing of family trios identifies novel genes in children with Rett syndrome (RTT) phenotype
phenotype: Rett-like phenotype; Features suggesting Rett syndrome diagnosis; Epileptic encephalopathy
diagnostic_reason: De novo heterozygous mutation identified by whole exome sequencing in MECP2-negative patient with Rett-like phenotype; previously linked to epileptic encephalopathy

citation: kcnb1 loss of function in zebrafish causes neurodevelopmental and epileptic disorders associated with γ-aminobutyric acid dysregulation (PMID: 40332468)
phenotype: impaired swimming behavior; epilepsy-like features; elevated locomotor activity in response to pentylenetetrazol (PTZ); increased bdnf mRNA expression; higher c-Fos fluorescence intensity in telencephalon; spontaneous and provoked epileptiform-like electrographic activity; γ-aminobutyric acid dysregulation; normal brain anatomy and neuronal circuit organization

citation: Abnormal cytoskeletal remodeling but normal neuronal excitability in a mouse model of the recurrent developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-susceptibility KCNB1-p.R312H variant (PMID: 39738805)
phenotype: severe cognitive deficit; compulsive behavior; neuronal damage in multiple brain areas; disrupted corticocortical and corticothalamic connectivity; aberrant glutamatergic vesicular transport; normal electrical properties of pyramidal neurons; marked differences in actin cytoskeleton remodeling

citation: Altered neurological and neurobehavioral phenotypes in a mouse model of the recurrent KCNB1-p.R306C voltage-sensor variant (PMID: 38485094)
phenotype: hyperactivity; altered susceptibility to chemoconvulsant-induced seizures; frequent long runs of slow spike wave discharges on EEG; altered neuronal excitability; slow spike and wave activity reminiscent of Lennox Gastaut syndrome

citation: Altered neurological and neurobehavioral phenotypes in a mouse model of the recurrent KCNB1-p.R306C voltage-sensor variant (PMID: 37034689)
phenotype: pronounced hyperactivity; altered susceptibility to flurothyl and kainic acid induced-seizures; frequent long runs of spike wave discharges on EEG

citation: Epilepsy and neurobehavioral abnormalities in mice with a dominant-negative KCNB1 pathogenic variant (PMID: 33132203)
phenotype: profound hyperactivity; repetitive behaviors; impulsivity; reduced anxiety; spontaneous seizures in homozygous mice; seizures induced by novel environments and handling; increased susceptibility to proconvulsant-induced seizures; abnormal interictal EEG activity including isolated spike and slow waves; genotype-dependent differences in KV2.1, KV2.2, and AMIGO-1 protein expression

citation: Oxidation of KCNB1 channels in the human brain and in mouse model of Alzheimer's disease (PMID: 30050035)
phenotype: improved working memory; reduced brain inflammation; reduced protein carbonylation; reduced intraneuronal β-amyloid (Aβ)

citation: Integrin-KCNB1 potassium channel complexes regulate neocortical neuronal development and are implicated in epilepsy (PMID: 36207442)
phenotype: impaired neuronal migration of glutamatergic neurons; migratory defects persisting into adult brains; disrupted neuronal morphology and synaptic connectivity; seizure phenotype; anxiety; compulsive behavior; impaired biochemical signaling of integrin-K+ channel complexes

citation: Kcnb1 plays a role in development of the inner ear (PMID: 33316259)
phenotype: defective otic vesicle expansion; abnormal otolith formation; impaired proliferation and differentiation of mechanosensory cells; defects of kinocilia and stereocilia; abnormal inner ear function; altered transcription of genes involved in K+ metabolism, cell proliferation, cilia development, and intracellular protein trafficking

citation: ASHG 2018 - Using zebrafish as a tool to model patient mutations of KCNB1 and its role in epilepsy (M.Y. Dennis, A. Colón-Rodríguez, K. Burbach, E. Ferino, M. Bader, P. Lein, L. Jao)
phenotype: increased activity (distance moved) in presence of PTZ in heterozygous and homozygous fish; no significant differences in body or head size compared to wildtype

citation: kcnb1 loss of function in zebrafish causes neurodevelopmental and epileptic disorders associated with γ-aminobutyric acid dysregulation. (PMID: 40332468)
summary: CRISPR/Cas9-generated kcnb1 knockout zebrafish (kcnb1+/- and kcnb1-/-) display impaired swimming behavior, epilepsy-like features, spontaneous and provoked epileptiform activity, and γ-aminobutyric acid dysregulation. kcnb1 is expressed in multiple CNS regions including neurons, oligodendrocytes, and microglial cells. Loss of function leads to increased bdnf mRNA expression and elevated c-Fos intensity in telencephalon upon PTZ exposure.

citation: Epilepsy and neurobehavioral abnormalities in mice with a dominant-negative KCNB1 pathogenic variant. (PMID: 33132203)
summary: KCNB1-G379R expressed in HEK293T cells shows dominant-negative effects, failing to induce endoplasmic reticulum-plasma membrane junctions and reducing their formation when co-expressed with wild-type KV2.1. This variant affects the non-conducting structural function of KV2.1 in organizing ER-PM junctions.

citation: Epilepsy and neurobehavioral abnormalities in mice with a dominant-negative KCNB1 pathogenic variant. (PMID: 33132203)
summary: Kcnb1G379R/+ and Kcnb1G379R/G379R mice show genotype-dependent differences in KV2.1, KV2.2, and AMIGO-1 protein expression levels. Mutant mice display profound hyperactivity, repetitive behaviors, impulsivity, reduced anxiety, spontaneous seizures, abnormal interictal EEG activity, and increased susceptibility to proconvulsant-induced seizures.

citation: Abnormal cytoskeletal remodeling but normal neuronal excitability in a mouse model of the recurrent developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-susceptibility KCNB1-p.R312H variant. (PMID: 39738805)
summary: Kcnb1R312H(+/+) mouse neocortical pyramidal neurons show normal electrical properties and ion-conducting functions compared to wild-type, but marked differences in actin cytoskeleton remodeling as measured by fluorescence recovery after photobleaching and biochemistry. This indicates the pathogenic mechanism involves non-ionic, structural functions of the channel.

citation: Functions and clinical significance of KCNB1 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. (PMID: 39893596)
summary: KCNB1 knockdown in KYSE70 and TE5 esophageal cancer cell lines inhibits cell proliferation, G2-M phase progression, migration, and invasion while inducing apoptosis. Microarray analysis shows KCNB1 regulates ephrin receptor signaling by suppressing EPHB1, EPHB2, and ERK1/2 expression, controlling cell proliferation through ERK1/2 regulation.

citation: Role of KCNB1 in the prognosis of gliomas and autophagy modulation. (PMID: 28144039)
sample_size: glioma cell lines and in vivo models
summary: KCNB1 induces autophagy in glioma cells through the ERK pathway, as confirmed by selective ERK1/2 inhibitor (U0126) and siERK1/2 studies. KCNB1 activation leads to increased apoptosis and reduced proliferation and invasion. In vivo studies show KCNB1 induces autophagy while inhibiting tumor growth and increasing survival.

citation: Gain-of-function enhancer variant near KCNB1 causes familial ST-depression syndrome. (PMID: 40208226)
sample_size: 67 FSTD patients (20 families), AC16 cardiomyocytes, human tissue
significance: perfect co-segregation with ECG phenotype, full penetrance
summary: A non-coding variant 18 kb downstream of KCNB1 creates a MEF2-binding site that enhances transcriptional activity and interacts with the KCNB1 promoter, as confirmed by 4C chromosome conformation capture in AC16 cardiomyocytes and human muscle tissue. dCas9-activator/repressor assays show KCNB1 is the only gene consistently regulated by this locus.

citation: A KCNB1 gain of function variant causes developmental delay and speech apraxia but not seizures. (PMID: 36618935)
summary: KCNB1 p.P17T variant shows gain-of-function properties in whole-cell patch-clamp recordings: increased current, rightward shifts in steady-state inactivation curve, and reduced sensitivity to guanxitoxin-1E blocker. This gain-of-function is associated with developmental delay and speech apraxia but notably without seizures.

citation: ASHG 2018 - Whole exome sequencing in epilepsy reveals significant gene burden of ultra-rare deleterious variants. (Y. Feng, on behalf of the EPI Collaborative)
summary: Gene-based burden tests in the Epi25 Consortium identified KCNB1 as significantly enriched for ultra-rare protein-truncating variants and damaging missense variants in epileptic encephalopathy patients compared to controls (OR=27.6, p=2e-05). KCNB1 was re-captured as an established epilepsy gene alongside SCN1A and STXBP1.

citation: ASHG 2018 - Dissecting heterogeneity of neurodevelopmental disorders using seed centric genetic modules. (J.C. Chow et al.)
sample_size: large cohorts of probands with neurodevelopmental disorders
significance: significant enrichment of de novo mutations within modules
summary: Modules seeded with epilepsy gene KCNB1 are significantly associated with long-term potentiation, synaptic vesicle cycle, and calcium signaling pathways. These modules show significant enrichment of de novo non-synonymous mutations and coding copy number variants in autism, intellectual disability, developmental disability, and epilepsy cohorts.

citation: ASHG 2016 - Genetic variants in KCNB1 are modestly associated with type 2 diabetes in American Indians from the Gila River Indian Community. (M. Traurig et al.)
summary: An intronic 16 bp deletion in KCNB1 (mAF=0.02) was associated with protection from type 2 diabetes in Pima Indians (OR=0.51, p=1.2×10-3). A common variant rs3827088 (mAF=0.31) showed association with increased T2D risk (OR=1.17, p=4.9×10-3), replicated in independent American Indian cohort (combined OR=1.18, p=2.5×10-4). Conditional analysis suggests independent effects of both variants.

citation: RNA-Binding Protein Hnrnpa1 Triggers Daughter Cardiomyocyte Formation by Promoting Cardiomyocyte Dedifferentiation and Cell Cycle Activity in a Post-Transcriptional Manner (PMID: 39559922)
phenotype: Inhibited cardiac regeneration; Worsened cardiac function in neonatal myocardial infarction model; Reduced Pbx1 expression regulation; Impaired cardiomyocyte dedifferentiation and cell cycle activity

citation: A PBX1-IL7R axis mediates liver fibrosis in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (PMID: 40885520)
phenotype: Myofibroblast-specific PBX1 depletion significantly attenuated liver fibrosis induced by CDAA-HFD; Liver injury and steatosis not influenced by PBX1 depletion; Reduced hepatic stellate cell activation

citation: Development and function of the mammalian spleen (PMID: 17226804)
phenotype: Asplenia or absent spleen; Defects in early splenic development and patterning; Reduced B cell populations involved in response to encapsulated bacteria; Increased susceptibility to infection with encapsulated bacteria

citation: Dynamic evolution of TCF3-PBX1 leukemias at the single-cell level under chemotherapy pressure (PMID: 39901941)
phenotype: TCF3-PBX1 fusion drives acute lymphoblastic leukemia development; CNS infiltration at relapse; Chemotherapy-resistant clones with altered apoptosis and signaling pathways; Upregulation of MYC signaling in persisting leukemic cells; Increased STAT3/5 phosphorylation upon preBCR stimulation

citation: The PBX1 lupus susceptibility gene regulates CD44 expression (PMID: 28257976)
phenotype: PBX1-d isoform expression in CD4+ T cells associated with systemic lupus erythematosus; Production of autoreactive activated CD4+ T cells; Reduced frequency and function of Foxp3+ regulatory T cells; Expansion of follicular helper T cells; Direct regulation of CD44 expression in T cells; Enhanced co-factor MEIS recruitment by PBX1-d over PBX1-b

citation: Meis2 controls skeletal formation in the hyoid region (PMID: 36247013)
phenotype: Severely reduced PBX1 expression in hyoid region; Aberrant hyoid apparatus development with complete skeletal chain from neurocranium to lesser horns; Ectopic loci of mesenchymal condensations; Ectopic cartilage and bone formation; Disinhibition of skeletogenesis; Elevated proliferation of cartilage precursors; Reduced HAND2 expression in hyoid region

citation: Cicero Predicts cis-Regulatory DNA Interactions from Single-Cell Chromatin Accessibility Data (PMID: 30078726)
summary: PBX1 is identified as a transcription factor that, together with MEIS1, mediates early opening of DNA elements bound by MYOD1 in differentiating myoblasts. These PBX1- and MEIS1-dependent elements are part of chromatin hubs that orchestrate gene regulation during myoblast differentiation.

citation: Rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus and primary Sjögren's syndrome shared megakaryocyte expansion in peripheral blood (PMID: 34462261)
sample_size: 119 treatment-naive patients (41 RA, 38 pSS, 28 SLE, 12 polyautoimmunity) and 20 healthy controls
summary: PBX1 is identified as an upregulated cell-lineage-specific transcription factor that, together with GATA1, TAL1, and GFI1B, defines a strong gene expression signature of megakaryocyte expansion in peripheral blood of patients with rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, and primary Sjögren's syndrome. PBX1 expression is associated with CD41b+CD42b+ and CD41b+CD61+ megakaryocyte subsets.

citation: The histone lysine acetyltransferase HBO1 (KAT7) regulates hematopoietic stem cell quiescence and self-renewal (PMID: 34724565)
summary: PBX1 is identified as a gene essential for hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) quiescence and self-renewal. Loss of HBO1 results in downregulation of Pbx1 expression in HSC-enriched populations, leading to abnormal HSC recruitment into the cell cycle and exhaustion of the HSC pool. PBX1 is part of a transcription factor network critical for HSC maintenance.

citation: Pre-B-cell leukemia transcription factor 1 contributes to liver fibrosis by enabling IL-7 signaling in HSC (PMID: 40080840)
summary: PBX1 is upregulated during hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation and mediates HSC-myofibroblast transition. PBX1 is transcriptionally activated by Notch3 signaling and directly activates IL7R (CD127) expression. PBX1 knockdown attenuates HSC activation in vitro and liver fibrosis in mice, while IL7R knockdown similarly impairs HSC activation.

citation: RNA-Binding Protein Hnrnpa1 Triggers Daughter Cardiomyocyte Formation by Promoting Cardiomyocyte Dedifferentiation and Cell Cycle Activity in a Post-Transcriptional Manner (PMID: 39559922)
summary: PBX1 is identified as a target of post-transcriptional regulation by Hnrnpa1, which promotes Mettl3 splicing to inhibit m6A-dependent Pbx1 degradation. Increased Pbx1 expression promotes cardiomyocyte dedifferentiation and cell cycle activity, triggering daughter cardiomyocyte formation and enhancing cardiac repair after myocardial infarction in mice.

citation: Development of combination therapies with BTK inhibitors and dasatinib to treat CNS-infiltrating E2A-PBX1+/preBCR+ ALL (PMID: 38598725)
sample_size: Primary ALL patient samples including E2A-PBX1+ cases
summary: PBX1 is part of the oncogenic E2A-PBX1 fusion protein arising from t(1;19) translocation in acute lymphoblastic leukemia. E2A-PBX1+ ALL cells are sensitive to combination therapy with dasatinib and BTK inhibitors, which reduces CNS infiltration and improves disease-free survival in mouse models.

citation: De novo, deleterious sequence variants that alter the transcriptional activity of the homeoprotein PBX1 are associated with intellectual disability and pleiotropic developmental defects (ASHG 2017)
summary: Seven patients with de novo deleterious PBX1 variants (missense mutations in or near the homeodomain, and truncating mutations) present with intellectual disability and pleiotropic developmental defects including external ear anomalies, heart malformations, diaphragmatic hernia, renal hypoplasia, and cryptorchidism. Functional studies show these variants impair PBX1 transactivation ability, nuclear translocation, and interactions with TALE/HOX cofactors, directly affecting transcription of PBX1 target genes.

citation: Interrogating the PBX-WNT-TP63 pathway in human nonsyndromic cleft lip/palate (ASHG 2013)
sample_size: 513 white non-Hispanic American families and 316 Hispanic families from Texas
significance: p=0.002 for PBX1 rs1044263 in Hispanic multiplex families
summary: PBX1 and PBX2 variants are associated with nonsyndromic cleft lip/palate (NSCL/P) in human populations. PBX1 rs1044263 shows association with NSCL/P in Hispanic multiplex families (p=0.002). PBX genes are part of a regulatory module (PBX-WNT-TP63-IRF6) controlling facial morphogenesis, with loss of Pbx genes in mice resulting in fully penetrant cleft lip/palate phenotype.

citation: A genome-wide association study reveals novel susceptibility loci for obesity in Saudi Arabs (ASHG 2013)
summary: PBX1 (PRE-B-Cell leukemia homeobox 1) on chromosome 1 is identified as a novel susceptibility locus for obesity in a genome-wide association study of 5,418 Saudi Arabs, with 94 genome-wide significant SNPs reaching p<1×10-5 threshold.

citation: Analysis of time-series embryonic diaphragm transcriptomes identifies Pbx1 as a candidate gene for diaphragmatic defects (ASHG 2011)
summary: Pbx1 is identified as a candidate gene for congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) through time-series transcriptomic analysis of embryonic mouse diaphragms. Pbx1 knockout mouse embryos at E15.5 exhibit a range of diaphragmatic defects, validating Pbx1 as a CDH-associated gene. Pbx1 is known as a facilitator of muscle differentiation and mesodermal patterning during embryogenesis.

citation: RAB17 promotes endometrial cancer progression by inhibiting TFRC-dependent ferroptosis (PMID: 39242574)
summary: RAB17 suppresses ferroptosis in endometrial cancer cells by inhibiting transferrin receptor (TFRC) protein expression through ubiquitin proteasome-dependent degradation. RAB17 expression increases under low-glucose conditions and promotes EC cell survival during glucose deprivation via the RAB17-TFRC axis.

citation: Single-cell RNA-seq and bulk-seq identify RAB17 as a potential regulator of angiogenesis by human dermal microvascular endothelial cells in diabetic foot ulcers (PMID: 37605780)
summary: RAB17 expression is significantly reduced in HDMECs from diabetic foot ulcer patients compared to healthy controls. RAB17 overexpression enhances angiogenesis, HIF-1α and VEGF-A expression, and diabetic wound healing partially through the MAPK/ERK signaling pathway.

citation: MAL2 and rab17 selectively redistribute invadopodia proteins to laterally-induced protrusions in hepatocellular carcinoma cells (PMID: 39813085)
summary: RAB17 expression promotes actin- and cholesterol-dependent protrusions and selectively redistributes invadopodia proteins to protrusion tips in a GTP-dependent manner. RAB17 interacts with MAL2 in a GTP-dependent manner and redirects trafficking of newly synthesized membrane proteins from the Golgi to induced protrusions.

citation: Downregulation of RAB17 have a poor prognosis in kidney renal clear cell carcinoma and its expression correlates with DNA methylation and immune infiltration (PMID: 37269962)
sample_size: KIRC tissues and normal tissues; cell lines
summary: RAB17 is low-expressed in KIRC tissues and cell lines. Downregulation of RAB17 correlates with unfavorable clinicopathological characteristics and worse prognosis. Six CpG sites show higher DNA methylation in KIRC tissues with negative correlation to RAB17 mRNA expression. RAB17 expression is negatively correlated with immune cell infiltration.

citation: Downregulation of Rab17 promotes cell proliferation and invasion in non-small cell lung cancer through STAT3/HIF-1α/VEGF signaling (PMID: 31841274)
summary: RAB17 knockdown promotes NSCLC cell proliferation, invasion, migration, and angiogenesis while suppressing apoptosis through activation of the STAT3/HIF-1α/VEGF pathway. RAB17 downregulation induces epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) by decreasing E-cadherin and increasing Vimentin and β-catenin.

citation: ALS2, the small GTPase Rab17-interacting protein, regulates maturation and sorting of Rab17-associated endosomes (PMID: 31959474)
summary: RAB17 localizes primarily to recycling endosomes in a Rab11-dependent manner. ALS2 interacts with RAB17 and regulates maturation of Rab17-residing nascent endosomes to EEA1-positive early endosomes. RABGEF1 functions as a GEF for RAB17, while ALS2 acts downstream to regulate endosomal maturation without GEF activity.

citation: LMO4 promotes OSCC progression by inducing RAB17 degradation and ferroptosis resistance (PMID: 41213908)
sample_size: OSCC tissues and cell lines; nude mouse xenograft model
summary: LMO4 promotes ubiquitin-proteasome-dependent degradation of RAB17 tumor suppressor in oral squamous cell carcinoma. LMO4-mediated RAB17 degradation enhances OSCC cell proliferation, migration, and ferroptosis resistance. RAB17 restoration reduces these malignant behaviors.

citation: Rab17 regulates apical delivery of hepatic transcytotic vesicles (PMID: 30256711)
summary: RAB17 is a monosumoylated protein that regulates basolateral-to-apical transcytosis in polarized hepatocytes. GTP-bound and sumoylated RAB17 are required for apical vesicle docking, and RAB17 GTP hydrolysis is required for vesicle delivery. RAB17 is a general component of transcytotic machinery for apically destined vesicle docking and fusion.

citation: Rab17 inhibits the tumourigenic properties of hepatocellular carcinomas via the Erk pathway (PMID: 25707355)
summary: RAB17 is reduced in HCC tissues (37.1% vs 64.6% in non-tumor tissue) and correlates with unfavorable variables including tumor size, differentiation, and metastases. RAB17 overexpression inhibits HCC cell proliferation, migration, and tumor growth while inducing G1 arrest. The anti-tumor effects are mediated through inhibition of the ERK pathway.

citation: A proteomic approach to identify endosomal cargoes controlling cancer invasiveness (PMID: 28062852)
summary: RAB17 knockdown selectively reduces cellular levels of Vamp8 (v-SNARE), which associates with RAB17 at late endosomes. RAB17 and Vamp8 regulate trafficking of neuropilin-2 (NRP2), a pro-invasive cargo. Reduced RAB17 or Vamp8 increases NRP2 cell surface expression and promotes transition from ductal carcinoma in situ to invasive phenotype.

citation: Peña-Münzenmayer et al. 2015 - Ae4 (Slc4a9) Anion Exchanger Drives Cl- Uptake-dependent Fluid Secretion by Mouse Submandibular Gland Acinar Cells (PMID: 25745107)
phenotype: Reduced salivation by 35% in Ae4(-/-) mice; Reduced Cl(-) uptake during β-adrenergic receptor activation; Reduced HCO3(-)-dependent Cl(-) uptake in acinar cells; Normal salivation in Ae2(-/-) mice; Nearly abolished Cl(-)/HCO3(-) exchanger activity in double Ae4/Ae2 knockout mice

citation: Peña-Münzenmayer et al. 2015 - A Mathematical Model Supports a Key Role for Ae4 (Slc4a9) in Salivary Gland Secretion (PMID: 29209914)
phenotype: Approximate 35% decrease in gland salivation in Ae4 deficient mice; Ae4 responsible for majority of secondary Cl(-) uptake; No impairment of salivation in Ae2 knockout mice

citation: Peña-Münzenmayer et al. 2017 - Activation of the Ae4 (Slc4a9) cation-driven Cl(-)/HCO(3)(-) exchanger by the cAMP-dependent protein kinase in salivary gland acinar cells (PMID: 34585968)
phenotype: Ae4-mediated Cl(-)/HCO3(-) exchanger activity increased in response to β-adrenergic receptor stimulation; PKA-dependent phosphorylation of Ae4 at S173 residue regulates activity; Ae4 critical for Cl(-) uptake across basolateral membrane of submandibular gland acinar cells

citation: Soleimani et al. 2012 - PAT-1 (Slc26a6) is the predominant apical membrane Cl-/HCO3- exchanger in the upper villous epithelium of the murine duodenum (PMID: 17170027)
phenotype: Cl(-)/HCO3(-) exchange activity reduced <5% in AE4(-) duodenum compared to wild-type; SO4(2-)/HCO3(-) exchange not affected in AE4(-) duodenum; AE4 minimal contributor to basal Cl(-)/HCO3(-) exchange in duodenal villous epithelium; PAT-1 is major contributor to apical membrane anion exchange in duodenum

citation: Terker et al. 2015 - Integrated compensatory network is activated in the absence of NCC phosphorylation (PMID: 25893600)

summary: iPSC-derived neurons from 6 STXBP1-RD patients showed reduced MUNC18-1 RNA and protein levels, dysregulation of synaptic proteins, and altered network activity patterns. Proteome-wide screening identified dysregulation of proteins related to synapse function and RNA processes, with patient clustering suggesting distinctive pathobiology.

citation: STXBP1 encephalopathy: Connecting neurodevelopmental disorders with α-synucleinopathies? (PMID: 31221716)
summary: STXBP1 (Munc18-1) controls the self-replicating aggregation of α-synuclein, a presynaptic protein involved in neurodegenerative diseases. STXBP1 functions as a molecular chaperone for α-synuclein, linking early-onset neurodevelopmental disorders with synucleinopathies.

citation: ASHG 2023 - α-Synuclein pathology in Drosophila melanogaster is exacerbated by haploinsufficiency of Rop: Connecting STXBP1 encephalopathy with α-synucleinopathies (T. Matsuoka et al.)
summary: In Drosophila, haploinsufficiency of Rop (STXBP1 homolog) exacerbates α-synuclein aggregation and pathology. Rop heterozygous flies showed increased insoluble α-synuclein, reduced dopamine neurons, and impaired motor function. Trehalose feeding reversed these phenotypes, demonstrating a molecular interaction between STXBP1 and α-synuclein in vivo.

citation: ASHG 2019 - Humanized STXBP1 animal models as a precision medicine approach to detecting pathogenicity in clinical variants (C. Hopkins et al.)
summary: Humanized C. elegans model with human STXBP1 inserted as replacement for unc-18 showed 100% rescue of function by electrophysiology (4-fold increase from knockout) and 100% rescue in thrashing assays. Pathogenic variants (p.R292H, p.R406H, p.R388X) showed quantifiable functional defects in heterozygotes, with p.R388X displaying dominant-negative activity.

citation: ASHG 2019 - Zebrafish modeling for the clinic: Rapid in vivo functional testing of patient variants for clinical applications (B. Jussila et al.)
summary: Zebrafish CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of stxbp1a (STXBP1 ortholog) was used to model pediatric epilepsy and encephalopathy. Morpholino knockdown coupled with transient mRNA rescue of variant cDNA enabled rapid functional assessment of pathogenic and VUS alleles in an intact animal model with ~95% conservation to human disease genes.

citation: Delineating clinical and developmental outcomes in STXBP1-related disorders (PMID: 38015929)
summary: Natural history study of 162 individuals with STXBP1-related disorders (1281 cumulative patient-years) revealed genotype-phenotype correlations: protein-truncating variants and deletions showed infantile spasms with seizure remission, while missense variants showed focal seizures and ongoing seizures. Age-dependent anti-seizure medication response was documented, with phenobarbital, levetiracetam, topiramate, and ACTH effective in first year of life.

citation: HSV-1 latency-associated transcript miR-H3 and miR-H4 target STXBP1 and GABBR2 genes (PMID: 37668872)
summary: HSV-1 LAT-encoded microRNAs miR-H3 and miR-H4 directly target STXBP1 3'UTR. Overexpression of miR-H3, miR-H4, or LAT significantly decreased STXBP1 gene expression (0.0593-0.84 fold reduction). Luciferase assays confirmed miR-H3 reduces Renilla expression through STXBP1 3'UTR binding (0.62-fold reduction).

citation: Identification of copper metabolism-related markers in Parkinson's disease (PMID: 39552415)
summary: STXBP1 was identified as one of 9 hub genes related to copper metabolism in Parkinson's disease through integration of differentially expressed genes, copper-metabolism-related genes, and immune cell-related genes. ROC analysis showed high predictive accuracy for PD, and STXBP1 was highlighted as a potential therapeutic target in PD pathology.

citation: ASHG 2023 - Comprehensive genomic analysis of a trios family study with an index child diagnosed with autism spectrum disorders (D. Manjegowda et al.)
summary: Whole-exome sequencing of 27 Indian trios with autism spectrum disorder identified STXBP1 as one of multiple genes with SNVs contributing to ASD. Pathway analysis revealed dysregulation of glutamatergic synaptic transmission, linking STXBP1 variants to synaptic dysfunction in ASD pathophysiology.
